visitor.rulesDescription: A few clear rules keep the challenge fair for every team.
rules: Create an original game and credit any third-party assets or sources.
Each team has 3–5 students from the same school and age category.
Students under 18 need parent or guardian consent.
The team must reach an average training completion of at least 80% to submit.
visitor.judgingDescription: Every project is assessed against the same weighted criteria.

faq.question: Who can register a school?
faq.answer: An authorised school representative, such as a principal, teacher or school coordinator, can submit the registration. The school must be approved before its teams participate.

faq.question: How many students can be on a team?
faq.answer: Each team includes 3–5 students from the same school and age category. A team leader coordinates the project and submits the final version.

faq.question: What does the training include?
faq.answer: The training includes seven sessions with attendance, practical assignments and a short quiz. Your team needs an average completion of at least 80% to become eligible for submission.

faq.question: What files do we need to submit?
faq.answer: Prepare a playable game build, a game design document, a presentation and screenshots. You can save project versions before the team leader submits and locks the final version.

faq.question: How does judging stay fair?
faq.answer: Eligible projects use the same weighted scoring criteria and blind judging. School and team identity are hidden during evaluation so judges can focus on the game itself.
